answer: To resist Sybil attacks in an agent economy, each identity must lock capital into a shared collateral reef whose size grows quadratically with the number of controlled identities. A new identity is only accepted after the operator posts an additional vine of stake through an on-chain bonding schedule; each extra identity triggers a ripple that multiplies the marginal deposit, so an attacker farming thousands of identities faces prohibitive capital and opportunity costs while honest single-identity agents pay only a modest flat entry fee. This makes mass duplication unprofitable.
